Attached are our redlines for the MSA and the short security questionnaire. Main points from legal/procurement:

- ProspectCo is requesting explicit ownership of model outputs generated from our customer content when those outputs are productized (i.e., shipped to end users or embedded in a product).

Elena — thanks for sending these over. Looping in Laura (legal), Ben (AE owning the deal), and Kimberly (product) so we can respond with concrete language/options.

Quick summary of Redwood's position and practical compromise paths we typically offer:

1) Output ownership: We generally grant customers rights to use and commercialize outputs for their internal products/features. For third-party productization (resell or redistribute), we ask for a productization license or a commercial add-on to cover retraining and liability exposure. We can propose explicit order-form language that differentiates "internal use" vs "productized/redistributed use."

2) Training/use of customer content: We will not use customer-provided content for model retraining by default unless the customer opts in. However, we do collect anonymized usage telemetry (latency, token distribution, error rates) to maintain service quality. For cases where customer wants ML improvements from their data, we offer a paid opt-in training program with clear data handling contracts.

3) Feedback license: We can offer a limited feedback license that allows Redwood to use non-personal, de-identified feedback to improve models, and we can carve out content that customers designate as not-for-training.

Proposed next steps:
- Laura and I will draft a tight set of clauses (MSA + Order Form language) with two options: a) default: telemetry allowed, training opt-in paid add-on; b) enterprise exception: customer-initiated training program with SOC2 + contractual safeguards.
- I'll share a redline by EOD tomorrow. If procurement needs an interim commercial term (e.g., price for training add-on), Ben will follow up.

Kimberly — are there product notes we should include re: how opt-out will appear in the Order Form (checkbox, API flag, etc.)?

Thanks — Rafael

Elena / Rafael / team — I reviewed ProspectCo's redlines and sketched alternate language that balances customer rights with Redwood's operational needs. Key elements in our proposed text (attached as Proposed_MSAText_v3.docx):

- Output Ownership: Customer retains ownership of outputs to the extent such outputs are derived solely from Customer Content and are not pre-existing Redwood Model outputs. We propose a definitional carveout to exclude: (i) Model outputs that are substantially similar to Redwood-delivered model behavior; and (ii) outputs generated by Redwood improvements unrelated to Customer Content. That prevents overbroad claims.

- Training / Feedback License: Redwood will not use Customer Content for model retraining unless Customer provides affirmative opt-in via the Order Form or a separate Training Agreement. Redwood may collect and use aggregated, non-content telemetry (e.g., token counts, latency metrics, anonymized error traces) to operate and improve the Service. Any use of Customer Content for retraining will be subject to data minimization, pseudonymization, and SOC 2+ obligations in the Training Agreement.

- Productization / Third-Party Distribution: For redistribution or resale of outputs, we propose a tailored Productization License term that requires a commercial add-on and includes indemnity cap alignment. For customers who only need internal consumption, the standard Order Form will permit internal product use without a separate fee.

- Escalation & Approvals: Enterprise exceptions (full-training access, exclusive output assignments) will require Legal + Security approvals and a timeline for remediation/testing.

If this approach looks acceptable in principle, Rafael/Ben can provide a commercial note (price for training add-on) and Kimberly can confirm how the opt-out/opt-in will be represented operationally (Order Form checkbox + API flag). I've attached the proposed MSA text for redline review.

1) Default stance (no extra fees): ProspectCo receives rights to use and commercialize outputs for internal products and customer-facing features. Redwood will not use Customer Content for model retraining by default.

2) Opt-in training program: If ProspectCo wants Redwood to use customer content to improve models (retraining, fine-tuning), we will provide a paid Training Agreement. That Agreement includes data handling safeguards (pseudonymization, retention limits, SOC2 evidence) and a clear schedule.

3) Productization add-on: Redistribution / resale beyond ProspectCo's own product usage requires a Productization License (commercial add-on). We can provide high-level pricing for that add-on; Ben will follow up with a commercial proposal in the next 48 hours.

4) Operational controls: Kimberly confirms the opt-out/opt-in will be implemented as an Order Form toggle and an API flag documented in the SOW.
